Ted Kaczynski: The FBI used the case identifier UNABOM (University and Airline Bombing) before his identity was known, resulting in the media naming him the "Unabomber".
In what year was Angelman syndrome discovered?
Angelman syndrome (AS) is a rare genetic disorder that affects approximately 1 in 15,000 individuals.

Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19 (Russian: Микоян и Гуревич МиГ-19; NATO reporting name: Farmer) is a Soviet second generation, single-seat, twinjet fighter aircraft.
Yakovlev MC-21: United Aircraft Corporation. The aircraft made its maiden flight on 28 May 2017 from Irkutsk.
Who is credited with discovering Lynx?
Lynx (constellation): Johannes Hevelius. Lynx is a constellation named after the animal, usually observed in the Northern Celestial Hemisphere.
Who is credited with discovering Newton's law of universal gravitation?
Newton's law of universal gravitation: Robert Hooke. This is a general physical law derived from empirical observations by what Isaac Newton called inductive reasoning.
Who is credited with discovering Pulsar?
Pulsar: Jocelyn Bell Burnell. This produces a very precise interval between pulses that ranges from milliseconds to seconds for an individual pulsar.
Who is credited with discovering Coma Berenices?
Coma Berenices: Conon of Samos. Coma Berenices is an ancient asterism in the northern sky, which has been defined as one of the 88 modern constellations.
A "classic organochlorine" insecticide once heavily used to treat seed and soil, it was banned in most countries by the 1990s after proving a persistent, bioaccumulating pollutant. What is it?
Aldrin is an organochlorine insecticide that was widely used until the 1990s, when it was banned in most countries.
Named for the Portuguese word for indigo shrub, this simplest aromatic amine smells of rotten fish, ignites into a smoky flame, and is a key precursor to polyurethane and dyes — what compound is it?
Aniline (From) is an organic compound with the formula C6H5NH2.

Around 1920, when the energy source of stars was a complete mystery, which English astrophysicist boldly and correctly guessed it was the fusion of hydrogen into helium — and lent his name to a natural ceiling on a star's brightness?
Arthur Eddington (28 December 1882 - 22 November 1944) was an English astrophysicist and mathematician.

An Arctic and sub-Arctic cetacean, it is one of two living members of the family Monodontidae and is also known as the white whale (the only cetacean regularly occurring with this color) and the sea canary for its high-pitched calls. What is it?
Beluga whale (Delphinapterus leucas), is an Arctic and sub-Arctic cetacean.

This semi-solid tissue inside the spongy portions of bones serves as the primary site of new blood cell production in birds and mammals, making up roughly 5% of an adult human's body mass — what tissue is it?
Bone marrow is a semi-solid tissue found within the spongy (also known as cancellous) portions of bones.
Its three-dimensional shape mimics adenosine closely enough to plug into the same receptors, blocking the brain's signal to wind down — which psychoactive substance is it?
Caffeine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant of the methylxanthine class and is the most commonly consumed psychoactive substance globally.

A cultivated variety of the same species as cabbage and broccoli, this vegetable's edible part is a dense head of undeveloped flower buds called the curd — one variety, Romanesco, grows its curds in stunning fractal spirals. Name this vegetable?
Charted in 1756 by Lacaille and named for the drafting tool that draws circles, this faint southern constellation is easily confused with the mariner's-compass constellation Pyxis. Which one is it?
Circinus is a small, faint constellation in the southern sky, first defined in 1756 by the French astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille.
This inorganic compound's blue crystalline pentahydrate form was historically called blue vitriol, while its anhydrous form is white and dissolves in water to form an octahedral complex. What is it?
Copper(II) sulfate is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula CuSO4.
Born at the Point McLeay Mission in 1872, this preacher and inventor who registered 10 patents is widely credited as the first Aboriginal Australian published author — who is he?
David Unaipon was an Aboriginal Australian preacher, inventor, and writer who has been widely credited as the first Aboriginal published author.
Fossils of this Late Devonian armored fish genus, among the earliest vertebrate apex predators ever, have turned up from Morocco to Poland to North America — which genus?
Dunkleosteus is an extinct genus of large arthrodire ("jointed-neck") fish that existed during the Late Devonian period, about 382-358 million years ago.

Often used to keep blood pressure from dropping during anesthesia, this stimulant has also been tried against asthma, obesity, and even narcolepsy — though it's no longer the preferred fix. What is it?
Ephedrine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant and sympathomimetic agent that is often used to prevent low blood pressure during anesthesia.
This type of anaerobic metabolism harnesses the redox potential of reactants like glucose to produce ATP without needing oxygen. What process is it?
Fermentation is a type of anaerobic metabolism that harnesses the redox potential of the reactants to make adenosine triphosphate (ATP) and organic end products.

Lasting anywhere from milliseconds to hours, these are the most luminous explosions in the universe after the Big Bang, sometimes triggered when massive stars collapse into black holes — what are they?
Gamma-ray burst (GRBs) are extremely energetic events occurring in distant galaxies that represent the brightest and most powerful class of explosion in the Universe.

Dating back roughly 250 million years to the early Triassic, these ground-dwelling herbivorous insects use powerful hind legs to leap away from danger and hatch as nymphs that molt five times — what's the insect?
Grasshopper are a group of insects belonging to the suborder Caelifera.
This naturally occurring molecule and medication is a powerful blood anticoagulant used to treat heart attacks and prevent clotting in dialysis machines and test tubes — what is it?
Heparin (UFH), is a medication and naturally occurring glycosaminoglycan.
In organisms whose total cell count is fixed at maturity, this cell-enlargement process drives nearly all further growth after the embryonic stage — what is it?
Hypertrophy is an increase in the size of individual cells.

In 1897, this British physicist showed that cathode rays were made of previously unknown negatively charged particles far smaller than atoms — the first subatomic particle ever identified. Who was he?
J. J. Thomson (18 December 1856 - 30 August 1940) was a British physicist.
This 19th-century French mathematician ranged across number theory, complex analysis, and mathematical physics — and his name now sits on a crater on the Moon. Who was he?

Joseph Liouville (24 March 1809 - 8 September 1882) was a French mathematician who worked on a number of different fields in mathematics, including number theory, complex analysis, and mathematical physics.
This broadly distributed genus of spiders is informally grouped under a nickname referencing marital loss, encompassing both black and brown members — what is its scientific name?
Latrodectus is a broadly distributed genus of spiders informally called the widow spiders, with several species that are commonly known as the true widows.
Prized as one of the most profitable seafood commodities in the coastal waters where it's caught, this clawed crustacean spends its life in crevices and burrows on the sea floor - which creature?
Lobster are malacostracan decapod crustaceans of the family Nephropidae or its synonym Homaridae.
Its bell-shaped flowers give way to yellow or orange berries, but this nightshade genus is better known by the folkloric root that inspired countless myths and superstitions — which genus?
Mandragora (genus) is a plant genus belonging to the nightshade family (Solanaceae).
This scientific field studies Earth's atmosphere and short-term weather phenomena, with a central focus on forecasting — name the discipline?
Meteorology is the scientific study of the Earth's atmosphere and short-term atmospheric phenomena (i.e., weather), with a focus on weather forecasting.
These small, non-vascular, flowerless plants form dense green clumps or mats in damp, shady spots — name this group of plants?
Moss are small, non-vascular flowerless plants in the taxonomic division Bryophyta sensu stricto.
This form of vitamin B3 is taken orally to treat pellagra without the skin-flushing side effect of niacin, and used as a cream to fight acne and reduce signs of aging skin — what's the compound?
Nicotinamide (INN, BAN UK) or niacinamide (USAN US) (IUPAC name: 3-pyridinecarboxoamide) is a form of vitamin B3 found in food and used as a dietary supplement and medication.
This flowering herb in the mint family, native to the Mediterranean, is sometimes called wild marjoram and is a staple of countless savory dishes. What is it?
Oregano (Origanum vulgare) is a species of flowering plant in the mint family, Lamiaceae.
First domesticated in Neolithic China and rarely living past twenty years, this deciduous fruit tree also produces a smooth-skinned variety commercially sold as a different fruit — which tree?
Peach (Prunus persica) is a deciduous tree that bears edible juicy fruits with various characteristics.
Whether captured electronically on a sensor or chemically on light-sensitive film, this art and practice of recording light also powers science and manufacturing — think photolithography. What is it?

Photography is the art, application, and practice of creating images by recording light, either electronically by means of an image sensor, or chemically by means of a light-sensitive material such as photographic film.
This autonomic nervous system disorder causes an abnormally large jump in heart rate — thirty beats per minute within ten minutes — simply from sitting up or standing. What condition is it?
Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) is a condition characterized by an abnormally large increase in heart rate upon sitting up or standing.
One of America's top rocketry and high-speed-flight experts, this engineer helped found engineering cybernetics before being deported to China in 1955. Who was he?

Qian Xuesen (December 11, 1911 - October 31, 2009; also spelled as Tsien Hsue-shen) was a Chinese aerospace engineer and cyberneticist who made significant contributions to the field of aerodynamics and established engineering cybernetics.
With Patrick Steptoe and Jean Purdy, this British physiologist pioneered the technique that led to the 1978 birth of Louise Brown, earning a 2010 Nobel Prize. Who was he?
Robert Edwards (physiologist) (27 September 1925 - 10 April 2013) was a British physiologist and pioneer in reproductive medicine, and in-vitro fertilisation (IVF) in particular.
Spanning continents from North America to temperate Asia, this genus covers the majority of the world's common bushy-tailed squirrels — which genus?
Sciurus (or) contains most of the common, bushy-tailed squirrels in North America, Europe, temperate Asia, Central America and South America.
About 0.01% of people are born with this condition, in which the heart typically ends up on the right side of the chest instead of the left — what is it?
Situs inversus is a congenital condition in which the major visceral organs are reversed or mirrored from their normal positions.
Also known as sea stars, roughly 1,900 species of these star-shaped marine invertebrates live on seabeds from warm tropics to icy polar oceans. What are they?
Starfish are a class of marine invertebrates generally shaped like a star polygon.
A staple corm across African, Caribbean, Oceanian, and Asian cultures, this root vegetable of the arum family is often likened to yams — what is it?
Taro (Colocasia esculenta) is a root vegetable.

Sitting at the organizational level between individual cells and a full organ, this biological term for a functional grouping of similar cells derives from a French word meaning 'to weave' — what is it?
Tissue (biology) is an assembly of similar cells and their extracellular matrix from the same embryonic origin that together carry out a specific function.

An oily, amber-colored liquid that's extremely non-volatile and therefore lingers in the environment, this organophosphorus compound was developed for chemical warfare and is lethal in doses of just tens of milligrams — which chemical agent?
VX (nerve agent) is an extremely toxic synthetic chemical compound in the organophosphorus class, specifically, a thiophosphonate.

This American physical chemist built ultra-sensitive Geiger counters and once worked on the Manhattan Project — but his 1960 Nobel came for a dating method that revolutionized archaeology and paleontology. Who was he?

Willard Libby (December 17, 1908 - September 8, 1980) was an American physical chemist noted for his role in the 1949 development of radiocarbon dating, a process which revolutionized archaeology and palaeontology.
A legendary Heian-era court diviner and astrologer, this figure lived 84 years free of illness, fueling belief in mystical powers — a Kyoto shrine bears his name today. Who is he?
A shortened-fuselage version of a popular narrow-body jetliner family, this aircraft entered service with Swissair in April 1996 and carries up to 156 passengers — which model?
Airbus A319: Airliner, shortened variant of the A320 family.

The brightest star in the constellation Aquila and a vertex of the Summer Triangle, this nearby A-type star spins so fast — about 286 km/s at its equator — that it bulges noticeably. Which star is it?
Altair: Brightest star in the constellation Aquila. Altair is the brightest star in the equatorial constellation of Aquila and the twelfth-brightest star in the night sky.
Its name comes from Latin words meaning 'to strangle' and 'chest,' and it describes pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart muscle — what is this condition called?
Angina: Chest discomfort due to disorder of the heart muscles.

Once mistaken for bacteria, this domain of single-celled organisms is now known to be the group from which eukaryotes evolved, distinguished by ether-linked cell membranes and a unique whip-like motility structure. What domain is it?
Archaea: Domain of organisms. Traditionally, Archaea included only its prokaryotic members, but has since been found to be paraphyletic, as eukaryotes are known to have evolved from archaea.
Sold as Lipitor, this first-line statin lowers cholesterol to fend off cardiovascular disease, with mild muscle aches among its better-known side effects — what's the drug?

Nicknamed the 'stone' or 'house' version of its family, this adaptable mustelid outcompetes its forest-specialist, pine-dwelling cousin in open habitats — and has even gone feral in North America. Which species is it?
Beech marten: Species of carnivore. It is listed as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List on account of its wide distribution, its large population, and its presence in a number of protected areas.
Recognizable by its angled wings and forked tail, this scavenging bird of prey is thought to be the world's most abundant raptor, with a global population topping six million — which bird?
Black kite: Species of bird. The black kite or fire kite (Milvus migrans) is a medium-sized bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors.
Cattle, bison, buffalo, and goat-antelopes like sheep and goats all belong to this family of cloven-hoofed ruminants with over 140 living species — what is it?
Bovidae: Family of mammals belonging to even-toed ungulates.
In 1930, which Indian physicist won the Nobel Prize for discovering that light changes wavelength when passing through a transparent material, becoming the first Asian to win a Physics Nobel?

Defined by a –COOH functional group attached to an R-group, and only partially dissociating in water, this general class of organic compounds includes fatty compounds and the building blocks of proteins — what is this functional class called?
Carboxylic acid: Organic compound containing a –C(=O)OH group.
Often called the Judas tree, this small deciduous redbud native to Southern Europe and Western Asia bursts into deep pink blossoms each spring — what species is it?

Caused by a bacterium spread through contaminated water and undercooked shellfish, this intestinal infection produces severe watery diarrhea that can trigger dehydration within hours — which disease is it?
Cholera: Bacterial infection of the small intestine.
Recognizable by a prominent crest and curved bill, this Australasian parrot family includes 21 species, the smallest of which is the cockatiel — which family of birds?
Cockatoo: Any bird in the family Cacatuidae.
These colonial marine invertebrates secrete calcium carbonate to build the hard skeletons that form tropical reefs — what are they?
Coral: Marine invertebrates of the subphylum Anthozoa.
Once sold under the brand name Flexeril and chemically similar to tricyclic antidepressants, this oral medication treats sudden muscle spasms — what's the drug?
Cyclobenzaprine: Muscle relaxant medication. It should not be used together with MAOIs.
Whether for an object, a process, or a system, this is the intentional concept or proposal created by a thinking agent, balancing purpose, aesthetics, and constraints — what single word names it?
Design: Plan for the construction of an object or system.
Despite its common names, this evergreen conifer isn't a true member of the pine, spruce, or hemlock genera, yet stands as the tallest species in its own family — what is it?
Douglas fir: Species of tree. It is native to western North America and is also known as Douglas-fir, Douglas spruce, Oregon pine, and Columbian pine.
This unit of energy equals the kinetic energy a single electron gains while crossing an electric potential difference of one volt — what is it called?
Sometimes abbreviated ETM, this antibiotic treats everything from respiratory infections to syphilis and is the eye ointment routinely dabbed on newborns to prevent eye infections. What is it?
Erythromycin: Antibiotic medication. Erythromycin (sometimes abbreviated ETM in reports) is an antibiotic used for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.
Native to the Iberian Peninsula and introduced to hundreds of locations worldwide, this grassland herbivore digs extensive burrow networks called warrens — what is it?
This genus of over 200 stinging insect species, Solenopsis, includes 'ginger' and 'tropical' varieties named for their painful bite and reddish coloring — what are they commonly called?
Fire ant: Genus of red ants.
A French economist who gave up accounting to lecture across France, he founded peace societies and the Inter-Parliamentary Union before sharing the very first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901. Who was he?
Frédéric Passy: French economist and pacifist (1822–1912)
Ranging from Baja California to Japan's coast, this cephalopod is the largest of its kind on Earth and a common aquarium favorite — which creature?
Giant Pacific octopus: Species of cephalopod. It can be found from the intertidal zone down to 2,000 m (6,600 ft), and is best-adapted to colder, oxygen- and nutrient-rich waters.
One of China's 'Four Great Domestic Fish,' this herbivorous freshwater species was later introduced to Europe and the US to control aquatic weeds — which fish?
Grass carp: Species of fish. This Asian carp is the only species of the genus Ctenopharyngodon.
This British mathematician has studied the math of dating and pandemics, delivered the Royal Institution's 2019 Christmas Lectures, and hosted BBC's 'Secret Genius of Modern Life' — who is she?
Hannah Fry: British mathematician and broadcaster (born 1984)
Found in trace amounts in modern gasoline blends, this colorless, six-carbon alkane boils at about 69°C and serves as a cheap, low-reactivity solvent — what is it?
A colorless gas that throws off white fumes the moment it meets moist air, it turns into a familiar strong acid once dissolved in water — which compound, formula HCl?
Hydrogen chloride: Chemical compound. Hydrogen chloride gas and hydrochloric acid are important in technology and industry.
Native to the subcontinent, the male of this bird species is called a peacock and sports a fan-shaped crest with a dazzling train of eyespot feathers used in courtship — which species?
Indian peafowl: Species of bird. The Indian peafowl (Pavo cristatus), also known as the common peafowl, or blue peafowl, is a species of peafowl native to the Indian subcontinent.
This American climatologist's 1988 Congressional testimony helped awaken the public to global warming, and he later turned activist — getting arrested more than once for the cause. Who is it?
A former Navy SEAL turned physician, this NASA astronaut flew to the International Space Station in 2025 as part of Expedition 72/73 after earning a Silver Star for valor in combat — who is he?
Jonny Kim: American astronaut, physician, and former U.S. Navy SEAL (born 1984)
The largest joint in the human body, it's a modified hinge that links the thigh to the lower leg via two separate joints — what is it?
Knee: Leg joint in primates. The knee is a modified hinge joint, which permits flexion and extension as well as slight internal and external rotation.

This small wild feline of South and Southeast Asia sports dark spots on a tawny coat and two stripes running from its eyes to its ears, and can live as high as 4,474 meters in the Himalayas — what is it?
Leopard cat: Small wild cat species. The leopard cat (Prionailurus bengalensis) is a small wild cat with dark spots on the tawny-coloured body and limbs.
This American WWII twin-engine, twin-boom fighter carried its pilot alone in a central nacelle and served as fighter-bomber, night fighter, and long-range escort — which aircraft was it?
Lockheed P-38 Lightning: American twin-engined fighter of WWII. The Lockheed P-38 Lightning is an American single-seat, twin-engined fighter aircraft that was used during World War II.
Occurring naturally as the mineral brucite, this poorly soluble white solid neutralizes stomach acid in a well-known antacid — which compound?
Magnesium hydroxide: Inorganic compound of formula Mg(OH)2.
Awarded a share of the 1954 Nobel Prize in Physics for his statistical interpretation of the wavefunction, this Göttingen-trained theorist helped found quantum mechanics — who is he?
Sold under the brand name Robaxin and developed in 1956, this centrally acting muscle relaxant treats short-term musculoskeletal pain but its exact mechanism remains unclear — what is it?
Methocarbamol: Medication for musculoskeletal pain. It may be used together with rest, physical therapy, and pain medication.

Flown by the Imperial Japanese Navy from 1940 to 1945 and code-named 'Zeke' by the Allies, this long-range carrier fighter combined agility, speed, and firepower unmatched early in WWII — which aircraft?
Mitsubishi A6M Zero: Japanese carrier-based fighter aircraft. The A6M was designated as the Mitsubishi Navy Type 0 carrier fighter (零式艦上戦闘機, rei-shiki-kanjō-sentōki), or the Mitsubishi A6M Rei-sen.
Which condition describes a total absence of speech that can result from injury, illness, trauma, or a developmental or neurological disorder — sometimes only temporary?
Muteness: Medical condition. In human development, muteness or mutism is defined as an absence of speech, with or without an ability to hear the speech of others.
This medical term for a birthmark or mole covers marks present at birth as well as ones that appear later in life — what is it called?
Nevus: Mole or birthmark; visible, circumscribed, chronic skin lesion.
Weighing up to 1,000 kg and resembling a fish head without a tail, this giant marine creature can be as tall as it is long when its fins are extended — what is it?
Ocean sunfish: Species of fish. The ocean sunfish (Mola mola), also known as the common mola, is one of the largest bony fish in the world.
This genus of highly sociable ruminants includes domestic sheep, believed to descend from the wild mouflon of central and southwest Asia — which genus?
Ovis: Genus of mammals. Ovis is a genus of mammals, part of the Caprinae subfamily of the ruminant family Bovidae.
This economist and longtime New York Times columnist was the sole winner of the 2008 Nobel for his work on new trade theory and economic geography. Who is he?
Sold under brand names like Sudafed PE, this nasal decongestant works as a selective alpha-1 adrenergic receptor agonist — what is the drug?
Phenylephrine: Decongestant medication. It is unclear whether its use during pregnancy and breastfeeding is safe.
First classified as its own fossil order in 1835, this group of Mesozoic marine reptiles thrived through the Jurassic before dying out at the end of the Cretaceous — what are they called?
Plesiosaur: Order of reptiles (fossil). The Plesiosauria or plesiosaurs are an order or clade of extinct Mesozoic marine reptiles, belonging to the Sauropterygia.
Caused by a single mutation in the LMNA gene, this rare disorder causes children to age dramatically faster than normal, with most not living past their twenties — which condition?
Progeria: Genetic disorder that causes early aging.
In Euclidean geometry, which fundamental relation says the square on a right triangle's longest side equals the sum of the squares on the other two — famously written a² + b² = c²?
Pythagorean theorem: Relation between sides of a right triangle.
This biological process comes in two forms — asexual, as seen in cloning, and sexual, which combines gametes carrying half the usual chromosome count — what's the process called?
Reproduction: Biological process. Reproduction (or procreation or breeding) is the biological process by which new individual organisms – offspring – are produced from their parent or parents.
With over three hundred species and tens of thousands of cultivars, this thorny, often-fragrant flowering shrub blooms in shades from white to pink, red, orange, and yellow — which plant?
This colorless, odorless nerve agent can kill within minutes of inhalation and was banned by the 1993 Chemical Weapons Convention — what is it?
Sarin: Chemical compound and chemical warfare nerve agent.
Drawing on fields from anthropology to epidemiology, this scientific discipline studies everything from sexual development in puberty to gender identity and paraphilias — which field of study?
Sexology: Scientific study of human sexuality.
Brittle, translucent, and found in nature as the mineral halite, this 1:1 compound seasons your fries and de-ices your roads. What is it?
Sodium chloride: Chemical compound with formula NaCl.
Known for a synchronized aerial swarming display called murmuration, this glossy-plumed bird family includes talkative mynas as members — which birds?
Starling: Family of birds. The Sturnidae are named for the genus Sturnus, which in turn comes from the Latin word for starling, sturnus.
This South African biologist made a tiny roundworm, C. elegans, the model organism for studying how bodies develop, sharing a 2002 Nobel for the work — who is he?
Sydney Brenner: South African biologist and Nobel prize winner (1927–2019)

Believing he'd been commanded to build the biblical Third Temple, this engineer single-handedly created an operating system written in a language he invented himself, despite later struggles with schizophrenia and homelessness — who was he?
Terry A. Davis: American computer programmer (1969–2018)
With the symbol Sn and atomic number 50, this metal emits a crackling 'cry' when bent and boasts more stable isotopes than any other element — which one?
Tin: Chemical element with atomic number 50 (Sn). A metallic-gray metal, tin is soft enough to be cut with little force, and a bar of tin can be bent by hand with little effort.
Nicknamed 'rabbit fever' and spread by ticks, deer flies or contact with infected animals, this bacterial infection causes fever, skin ulcers and swollen lymph nodes — what is it?
Tularemia: Infectious disease caused by the bacterium Francisella tularensis.
Found only in the northern Gulf of California, this porpoise is the smallest living cetacean and is critically endangered due to bycatch from an illegal fishery — which species?
Vaquita: Endangered species of porpoise. The vaquita ( və-KEE-tə; Phocoena sinus) is a species of porpoise endemic to the northern end of the Gulf of California in Baja California, Mexico.

Also known as 'wet brain,' this neurological condition results from a severe thiamine deficiency and classically presents with confusion, poor coordination, and eye movement problems — which condition is it?
Wernicke encephalopathy: Medical condition. The condition is part of a larger group of thiamine deficiency disorders that includes beriberi, in all its forms, and alcoholic Korsakoff syndrome.
This Egyptian archaeologist twice served as his country's Minister of Tourism and Antiquities and has dug at sites from the Nile Delta to the Western Desert — who is he?
What is the chemical symbol for bromine?
The symbol for bromine is Br. Bromine is a chemical element; it has symbol Br and atomic number 35.
Tantalum is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for tantalum is Ta. Tantalum is a chemical element; it has symbol Ta and atomic number 73.
